title: OpenMarket
summary: Multi-agent marketplace where proof decides who wins
body: What if marketplaces rewarded the best product instead of the best marketing? OpenMarket (in research preview), is a multi-agent marketplace where sellers pitch, competitors challenge their claims, and independent truth agents verify the evidence as they compete to earn a buyer's sale. Here, claims don’t count just because they’re written on a product page. They have to survive scrutiny and be proven.

title: Knockin'
summary: Turns your static bio into an AI business card that replies
body: Knockin turns your bio into an AI business card people can chat with. Add your work, links, and content. It learns what you do and answers questions in your voice. Visitors can book time with you right away, even when you’re away. Knockin remembers who stopped by, so you know who to follow up with. This cuts down on back and forth and gives both sides more context before a call.

title: Relaticle
summary: Open-source CRM with approval-gated AI writes
body: Most CRMs bolt AI on. Relaticle is built agent-first: any MCP client gets 37 first-party tools over OAuth, with workspace custom fields in each agent's schema automatically. The in-app assistant is stricter: every write is a proposal showing the exact change, approved record by record. Self-host everything under AGPL, including local inference with Ollama. Free forever self-hosted; Cloud is flat per-workspace pricing, not per-seat.

title: Jupitrr Cut
summary: Open source app for recording vids with a teleprompter
body: Jupitrr Cut is an open-source mobile app for recording polished talking-head videos. Use the built-in teleprompter to read line by line, retake anything, and automatically remove silences. Export a finished video without touching a timeline. Record the video. Skip the edit. Add captions and B-roll later with Jupitrr AI—completely optional. No account wall. GPL-3.0 licensed, with the APK on GitHub and one-tap updates through the App Store and Google Play.

title: Tables.so
summary: AI that finds, qualifies and enriches your next customer
body: Finding new customers takes way too long and most of that time goes into work nobody wants to do. So we built Tables. You write who you are looking for in normal language and Tables goes through 300M+ verified contacts, looks into each one and answers the questions you actually care about. You get a scored list with emails, phone numbers and the sources behind every answer, so you can check it. Syncs with HubSpot, Pipedrive and Attio, and works on LinkedIn and inside Claude.

body:
I wrote recently about how the collection of good, fruitful open problems is now being mined in a non-renewable fashion, leading to the potential scenario of these problems becoming scarce. [...]

We have now seen that even the rumor of someone working on a problem can trigger a massive amount of AI-powered effort to flatten it before the original research project has time to reach its full potential. The incentives may now be pointing in the direction of no longer sharing any promising research directions with the broader community, which would reverse centuries of traditions of open science and do serious long-term damage to the future of the field.

—

Introducing ChatGPT Images 2.5

OpenAI's image generation models are apparently used "more than 3 billion images across ChatGPT Images and the GPT‑Image models in the API". This latest release improves their instruction-following ability across multiple turns, responds faster, and "is better at preserving the subjects in your reference photos".

There are two new model IDs in the API: gpt-image-2.5-sunburst and gpt-image-2.5-flare. Based on this I think Sunburst is the stronger option:
